headline: Mostly quiet weather through Friday, with fog early Tuesday, gusty east winds and a few showers in the south half of western Washington on Wednesday, before a wetter, stormier pattern returns this weekend into next week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Monday night turns drier, with leftover showers mostly staying offshore after a few moved inland across the Olympic Peninsula this evening. With light winds and clearing skies, fog forms overnight, first in the South Sound and Chehalis River Valley (around Olympia) and then spreading into other parts of Puget Sound, possibly thick for a few hours early Tuesday; Sea-Tac has about a 10% chance of dense, low fog between 4 and 6 AM. The fog clears by mid-morning Tuesday as a breeze off the ocean picks up, and Tuesday highs are mostly in the low 50s.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: A deep storm system off the coast slides south Tuesday night into Wednesday, keeping most of its rain south of western Washington, but it swirls some spotty showers into the southern half of the area and along the coast on Wednesday. East winds pick up, especially through the Cascade passes and gaps, with a 40–60% chance of gusts over 35 mph Wednesday morning. Wednesday is a bit cooler, with highs in the upper 40s to low 50s (mid 40s possible on the coast and in the southwest interior) and lows in the low to mid 30s.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thursday and Friday turn drier as the storm moves off to the south, though fog is likely in places Friday morning. Over the weekend a new storm system drops down from the Gulf of Alaska and parks along the coast, spinning light rain showers back into the area. Computer models point to a wetter, more active first half of next week with several storms moving through, though no rain amounts are given yet. River flooding isn't expected for the next several days, but chances rise again early next week, mainly on the Skokomish River.

coast: Seas of 14–16 ft on the coastal waters Monday evening ease to 10–12 ft by Tuesday morning. Winds increase Tuesday and turn offshore Tuesday night, funneling east through the Strait of Juan de Fuca at 25–30 knots in the central and western Strait (small craft advisories likely) and near Grays Harbor. On the outer coastal waters there's a 70–90% chance of gale-force gusts, and a Gale Warning runs from 1 PM Tuesday to 4 AM Wednesday; gale gusts may briefly reach the inner waters near the west entrance of the Strait and Grays Harbor County, and seas build back to 12–15 ft Tuesday night into early Wednesday. Small Craft Advisories are up for the Grays Harbor Bar until 4 AM Tuesday, the west entrance of the Strait until midnight tonight, and the coastal waters until 1 PM Tuesday. Wednesday through Friday are calmer on the water before things turn active again this weekend.
watch_for: Early-morning fog Tuesday (and again Friday) around Puget Sound, the South Sound and the Chehalis Valley.
Gusty east winds out the Strait of Juan de Fuca Tuesday night and through the Cascade passes Wednesday morning.
How wet next week gets: several storms are expected, and river flooding chances rise early in the week, mainly on the Skokomish.
confidence: Forecasters are fairly confident in Tuesday's fog-then-dry weather and in strong offshore winds Tuesday night (70–90% odds of gales offshore), less certain about exactly where Wednesday's spotty showers fall, and describe the weekend and next week only in general terms as wetter and more active.
